newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen easing at the open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen easing at the open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to give up more ground at the market open on Tuesday, extending Monday's decline, as weakness in the technology sector and interest rate worries weighed on markets.

"I think we're set to open a bit lower," Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co, said. "The market is nervous about the economy reaccelerating and about interest rate concerns."
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was off 3.70 points at 842.50 while the long bond was unchanged at a 6.90 percent yield.
The technology sector was set to weaken after both Seagate Technology Inc and Cabletron Systems Inc warned of below-estimate quarterly results, analysts said.
"Techs have had it on the upside and they should come under pressure," Metz said. "There is a switch going on into underexploited, secondary areas and that should continue."

Cabletron's stock sank to 35 from last night's closing price of 45-3/4 in early third market trade, on news it expected to report first quarter income of about $0.37 per share versus the First Call consensus estimate of $0.50 per share. Other networking stocks also weakened.
